name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Thompson holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising and cash advantage
Markets price Thompson near 96 percent; no polls or ratings contradict
Long-serving incumbent faces a little-known, underfunded challenger
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean, Thompson's long incumbency, and a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage leave Bilger with no visible path, and prediction markets price the race near 96 percent Republican with no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending on Bilger or polling showing a dramatically improved Democratic national environment could narrow the margin, though nothing currently indicates either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
PA-15 is a heavily Republican district in north-central Pennsylvania, and Republican Glenn Thompson has held the seat since 2009. He is seeking another term against Democrat Ray Bilger, a first-time challenger with limited resources. Thompson has raised roughly ten times as much money as Bilger and holds a large cash advantage, while outside groups have shown little interest in the race on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this contest, but prediction markets put Thompson's chances around 96 percent. The district's strong Republican lean, Thompson's long incumbency, and the wide financial gap all point in the same direction. A Democratic win would require a dramatic, district-specific shift well beyond anything visible in the available evidence, so the race is rated Safe Republican.
